sampling_model.design: A uniform balanced pilot split, balanced complete randomization on \(S_m\), and a pilot-measurable positive-support exact-alpha ellipsoidal mixture on \(T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}=S_m^c\), compared with the full-array oracle on \(T_n^{\mathrm{full}}\).
sampling_model.units: A deterministic triangular array of \(n\) units with complete bounded baselines known before assignment and fixed realized potential outcomes for design-based inference.
sampling_model.treatment: All \(Q=2^{K_f}\) combinations receive equal wave-specific counts.
sampling_model.overlap: The fixed mixture weight \(\eta>0\) gives every balanced assignment positive probability and every unit--combination inclusion positive probability.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Pilot outcomes identify \(\beta=(\rho,\lambda)\); the oracle coordinate is estimated after efficient projection on the nuisance score, the baseline array contributes no likelihood information, and the random-complement oracle map converges with three quotient derivatives in probability over the pilot split to the same \(G_{\infty}\) as the full-array map.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The learned factorial rerandomization procedure achieves the same first-order asymptotic precision as its oracle under suitable conditions.
The pooled binary-arm conditional-minimax-regret plan uses an \(n^{2/3}\) pilot and is approximately worst-case optimal.
The two-stage Bayesian rerandomization procedure learns covariate importance from a pilot and improves first-order precision.
Inverse inclusion weighting gives unbiased estimation under unequal-probability sampling without replacement.
The Horvitz--Thompson estimator is quadratically mean consistent under broad general designs.
Finite-population random partitions obey joint central limit theorems for multiple treatments and vector outcomes.
Fixed symmetric factorial rerandomization yields a truncated-Gaussian joint limit and conservative confidence regions.
Finite-population Gaussian approximation supports large-sample inference for best-choice Mahalanobis rerandomization.
Symmetric rerandomization preserves unbiasedness of ordinary factorial-effect estimators.
Quadratic-form rerandomization criteria admit fixed-geometry precision comparisons and a minimax Euclidean choice.
Sequential superpopulation experiments have first-order semiparametric efficiency bounds under adaptive assignment.

body.tldr: A balanced pilot learns which covariate imbalances matter for a vector of factorial effects, and an exact-alpha positive-support ellipsoidal mixture uses that information in the main wave. The full-array oracle map and the random-complement oracle map, the latter in probability over the pilot split, converge uniformly with three quotient derivatives to one \(G_{\infty}\); its continuous coarea boundary covariance defines \(B(\beta)=\operatorname{tr}\{\Gamma(\beta)I_{\mathrm{eff}}(\beta)^{-1}\}\). Relative to the matching full-array empirical oracle, the exact-inclusion pooled Horvitz--Thompson estimator has the sharp uniform contrast \(A(\beta)m/n^2+B(\beta)/(nm)\). Any pilot sequence whose minimax excess-risk ratio to the best admissible balanced size tends to one has the unique scale \(m/\sqrt n\to t^{\star}\), with a global constant certified by at most two active parameter values. The open mathematical core is a lattice- and tie-uniform finite-randomization comparison that validates these coefficients for unequal exact inclusions and arbitrary pilot-measurable actions.

project_justification.gap: The closest factorial procedure reaches its oracle only at first order and explicitly leaves the learning-sample proportion open. Binary-arm pilot theory gives a different global boundary rate, while general Horvitz--Thompson and rerandomization theory stop at exact unbiasedness, consistency, or first-order Gaussian limits.
project_justification.niche: A fixed complete baseline array and a connected full-dimensional conditional-outcome chart isolate a locally regular design problem in which pilot opportunity cost and oracle-action curvature coexist at the \(n^{-3/2}\) scale.
project_justification.fill: The project derives a common experiment-indexed oracle limit with uniform derivative convergence, defines its boundary curvature by continuous coarea disintegration, obtains both risk coefficients, proves the local arbitrary-action lower bound and efficient upper bound, controls exact ties and unequal inclusions, and converts the expansion into a unique global pilot constant through an explicit asymptotic-minimax risk ratio.

body.related_work: Han and Deng's Theorem 8 supplies the closest factorial-vector sample-splitting architecture and first-order oracle equivalence; the present theorem targets the smaller risk terms that their Section 6 leaves unresolved within the explicitly narrower likelihood-rich subclass recorded in Proposition 1. Yamin's Appendix E supplies the pooled opportunity-cost versus action-regret accounting, but its binary Neyman-allocation boundary class yields an \(n^{2/3}\) plan and informs rather than determines the local factorial result. Liu, Han, Rubin, and Deng optimize prior-integrated asymptotic variance and motivate covariance-aware rerandomization, but do not give a frequentist nuisance-efficient local minimax boundary. Horvitz and Thompson provide the exact inverse-inclusion identity, and Delevoye and Sävje provide broad consistency; neither gives a pilot-conditional second-order factorial risk expansion. Li and Ding's random-partition theorem and Li, Ding, and Rubin's truncated-Gaussian factorial law are the first-order finite-population foundations. Wang and Li quantify Gaussian approximation under selective rerandomization, but their result does not control a moving exact-alpha boundary at the proposed risk scale. Branson, Dasgupta, and Rubin establish the symmetric factorial benchmark to which the exact-inclusion estimator reduces. Menon, Chakrabarti, and Nerella document the practical sequence of factorial product-development cycles; the present consumer claim is prospective and additionally requires preregistered future baselines and a stable rich response family.
body.technical_internal_limitation: An exact four-unit nonsymmetric score example has positive support, acceptance probability \(137/1000\), inclusion probabilities \(1/16\) and \(7/16\), and zero Horvitz--Thompson bias, yet its empirical-oracle exact risk is discontinuous as a score coordinate crosses zero. Thus smooth outcome likelihoods do not justify continuity of finite score orderings. The theorem must use worst-case suprema and prove that any lattice discontinuity is below \(m/n^2+1/(nm)\); it may not assume finite-risk continuity or finite maximum attainment.
body.honest_scope: Exact Horvitz--Thompson centering, the \(O(|T|^{-1})\) one-wave risk bound under positive support, the continuous-coarea Gaussian boundary Hessian calculation, and the deterministic convex-envelope certificate have verified proof routes in the presolve evidence but remain marked to prove in this proposal core. Uniform convergence of \(G_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}\) and its first three quotient derivatives is deterministic conditional on the complete baseline array; the corresponding convergence for \(G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}\) is in probability over the uniform pilot split. The central uniform finite-randomization expansion, exact-inclusion perturbation bound, arbitrary-action localization, and nuisance-efficient local minimax transfer are open. The probability-one realized population class is a strict subclass of Han and Deng's published finite-population class because efficient pilot information is not defined on their unparameterized arrays; the achievability claim is not asserted beyond this subclass. Rank crossings, weak oracle signals, informative random baselines, finite parameter catalogues, and shifted noncentered actions are excluded. Under treatment-label symmetry, the estimator and first-order law reduce to the established ordinary factorial rerandomization result.
